# A canceled touch commits the drag over a valid drop target

Please comment to claim before starting and check the current assignees and linked PRs. A small public Board example reproduces the problem.

## Context

On Engine `7cd0d6618e`, open the [basic Task Board](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/tree/7cd0d6618e938ae6a79eb5ab47161bf9086e07fb/examples/board/basic). In touch-enabled Chromium, long-press card 1 in Backlog and drag it over Ready. Its record still reads Backlog while held. Send a trusted `Input.dispatchTouchEvent({type: 'touchCancel', touchPoints: []})` through CDP. The browser emits `pointercancel` with no `pointerup`. The record nevertheless changes from Backlog/order 1000 to Ready/order 0 and fires one `cardMove`. Repeating with `touchEnd` produces the same change.

A second consumer exposed the consequence across widgets. A canceled touch over a valid Scheduler forecast created a 06:00 booking and updated the Gantt installation time to 16:45. Routing the same native cancellation through the existing Main cancellation path kept the booking count at zero. [Kiln Room experiment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/21664#discussioncomment-19789978)

## The problem

The platform can take an active pointer away before the user releases it. At a valid target, the current terminal commits the user’s pending edit. Releasing outside the target or testing only that the drag proxy disappears misses the data change.

## The architectural reality

The [Pointer sensor](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/7cd0d6618e938ae6a79eb5ab47161bf9086e07fb/src/main/draggable/sensor/Pointer.mjs#L160-L179) emits `drag:end` with the last known point for an engaged [pointercancel](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/7cd0d6618e938ae6a79eb5ab47161bf9086e07fb/src/main/draggable/sensor/Pointer.mjs#L307-L313). [Main DragDrop](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/7cd0d6618e938ae6a79eb5ab47161bf9086e07fb/src/main/addon/DragDrop.mjs#L299-L361) still has the native event, hit-tests the point and forwards an ordinary end. Its existing `cancelDrag` routes a cancellation to the owner. The [captured-touch component test](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/7cd0d6618e938ae6a79eb5ab47161bf9086e07fb/test/playwright/component/dashboard/DockSplitterIframePane.spec.mjs#L423-L442) checks one terminal and an idle sensor. Both pass when the card moves.

## The fix

Preserve the difference between platform interruption and intentional release at the shared gesture boundary while retaining the pointer cleanup. The Board and other consumers should receive one cancellation and no committing drop.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On the public Board path above, native cancellation over Ready leaves the card's original column and order intact, emits no move, removes the proxy and releases capture.
- [ ] On the same path, a normal release commits exactly one move. A new gesture immediately after cancel can complete.
- [ ] Cover the stored outcome with trusted touch input and preserve the existing terminal-count, Escape, and lost-release coverage. A canceled gesture with an active resize follows the existing cancellation semantics.

## Out of scope

Changing touch arming thresholds, edge scrolling, or Board-specific sorting rules. Avoid individual consumer patches that would leave other drop targets exposed.

Prior art includes [the Pointer Events migration](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/17889), which covered termination and capture cleanup. The latest 20 open issues, open and closed cancellation searches, current PRs, recent lane claims, Memory Core and my assignments yielded no owner for committing on platform cancel. The open backlog stood at 78.
